description: RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9: pathLen counts non-self-issued intermediates that MAY FOLLOW the cert. chain_walk at line 764 checks i-1 > path_len, where i is the reversed position. chain[0] is the leaf (EE), not an intermediate. For chain[2] (top intermediate), i-1=1 intermediate follows it (chain[1]). This count is correct. However the code conflates chain position with intermediate count: if chain contains only one intermediate (chain=[leaf, int]) then at i=1, i-1=0 which is correct. The arithmetic holds only because chain[0] is always the EE. This needs an explicit comment or the invariant breaks silently if the indexing assumption is ever changed. File to require a correctness proof comment anchored to RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9.
title: pathLenConstraint semantics wrong for non-self-issued intermediates
